summary: Contract 25.4 (Electricite biome) implemented and verified in a built player. ElectricComposite (thin graph + ElectricComposite.hlsl): blue-black circuit-board ground with a faint hex trace/via grid that brightens and takes the nearby player's tint close to territories, a cool neon arena edge; territories as dimmed neon plasma with a slowly flowing hex pattern, a bright neon rim, crawling micro arcs (jagged contour re-rolled at 12 Hz on moving segments) and occasional lightning arcs hopping along the border (random spot per 3.2 u cell every 0.38 s), plus a colored outer glow; live-wire threads (neon body at the contract visible width, thin white-hot core displaced by a jagged offset re-rolled at 17 Hz, colored glow halo, same-color fusion at necks); fill = a crackling discharge of branching lightning driven by _PIO_RevealTime with a bright leading edge, then one hex pulse; dashed marching neon pocket lines (flat, no rim, no flow); elimination = short circuit through _PIO_PlayerFade (shape kept, surge, 9 Hz half-contrast flicker, black out). Fetch budget on Medium: 5 without actors, 6 with actors. ElectricBead: pearls as solid plasma orbs (white-hot core, 4 crackling filaments, brighter shell, colored glow, never a ring); droplets, evaporating beads and splash drops as flickering spark dots and streaks (the graph adds a world Position input for per-bead seeds). ElectricOverlay: contract shapes 0-5 restyled as neon (ring with crawling arcs, glow halo, neon chevron with dark outline, jagged spark star, crackling flash ring, disc) plus ElectricFx shapes 6-10 (bolt, cable strip, glow strip, spark, packet). ElectricFx: orb-to-territory arcs within 1.5 u (short arcs onto the territory at home), the current packet (white-blue head in an emissive halo, glow tail along the wire, shed sparks) exactly on the retraction front, the dim grey dead cable from the cut point to the front under the spark-dot droplets, the dead-wire fizzle on a saved chased return, branching fill bolts growing from the return point over FillDuration, and the short-circuit burst (22 sparks, radiating arcs, flash); capped at 200 quads. ElectricSfx: low mains hum ambience (4 s seamless loop), spark tick on exit, power thunk on return, crackle burst on fill, zap on cut, rising 110 Hz buzz tension loop (0.5 s seamless), discharge on catch, fizzle for loop lost. Verification: SetupAndCompile PASS (ShaderCheck 12 shaders, the 3 electric graphs compile 6 URP passes), EditMode 419 tests 0 failures 2 skipped, PlayMode 8/8, BuildWindows -buildOut Build/ELEC, player probe -biome electric PASS (33 checks, hash 246577239DE179C4 equal to the liquid probe on the same build, avgMs 16.75 at the 60 fps cap, tier High), DevShot PASS at High, Medium and Low with zero exceptions. Screenshots in docs/waveB/shots/ELEC (High, the PC default with bloom) and docs/waveB/shots/ELEC/medium (Android default tier, no bloom): electric_menu = menu over the electric attract match (pink plasma territory with neon rim and a live wire behind the biome cards); electric_ThreadOut = the human's live wire leaving its hex-plasma territory, jagged white core in a pink neon body and glow, the plasma orb with filaments at the tip, the neck fused with the rim; electric_MidFill = the capture filling: branching lightning bolts from the return point and the crackling discharge over the freshly revealed cells with a bright leading edge, the rest of the territory already showing its hex pattern, the thread ghost below; electric_CutDroplets = after the cut: the white-blue packet at the retraction front (partly under the tutorial pointer ring), the dead grey cable with flickering spark dots behind it and shed sparks, the yellow attacker's live wire, the crackling cut flash ring; electric_SavedReturn = saved chased return: the dead wire fizzling out (grey cable with dying spark dots), the toast 'Rentre 0,3 s avant l'etincelle : boucle perdue', no fill; electric_PocketPending = dashed pink neon pocket lines over the cyan rival territory, home pink territory with full hex plasma and rim clearly different, four distinct neon colors, orb arcs from the pink orb to its territory; electric_Caught = the short-circuit burst (white and pink sparks, radiating arcs) where the human is caught, the dying human wire without its white core, violet live wire, orbs as solid glowing balls; electric_results = results over the electric match.
api_additions: Fixed GUIDs: ElectricComposite.hlsl 67a2502f5eeb4a68861aa3d7ba7b5509, ElectricComposite.shadergraph a45dff4472614b17955b4bc35be14ae7, ElectricBead.hlsl faa893c44e6045f1b40ed0abffb7459b, ElectricBead.shadergraph 13c5cf6391084f80a876f3248efc0ebe, ElectricOverlay.hlsl 05cd1997f93447179224c05ccb3853da, ElectricOverlay.shadergraph 6f3394cd9c924af783862c9b4cfbd2b6 (graph object id prefixes e4 / e5 / e6).

HLSL functions PIO_ElectricCompositeSG_float/_half(VertexColor, UV1), PIO_ElectricBeadSG_float/_half(VertexColor, UV0, UV1, UV2, WorldPos), PIO_ElectricOverlaySG_float/_half(VertexColor, UV0, UV1, UV2); all helpers prefixed PIOE_ (no collision with LiquidComposite helpers).
ElectricBead.shadergraph has one extra input node: Position (World) -> custom function slot WorldPos (id 6). Same vertex data as Bead otherwise.

ElectricOverlay shapes 6 Bolt (a seed, b aspect halfY/halfX, c core half width in u), 7 Cable and 8 Glow (strip meshes: UV0 = along, cross -1/+1, half width, level), 9 Spark (a intensity), 10 Packet (a intensity); used only by ElectricFx. Halo (shape 1) reads c as extra emission 0..1 (the shared views pass 0, unchanged output).

ElectricFx public consts MaxParticles 200, ArcReach 1.5, ShapeBolt 6, ShapeCable 7, ShapeGlow 8, ShapeSpark 9, ShapePacket 10, QueueCables 3000, FizzleSeconds 0.45, CatchFadeSeconds 0.25, FillBoltFade 0.2, BurstSeconds 0.6, PacketTailLength 0.75, CableHalfWidth 0.045, CableSampleSpacing 0.15; properties LastQuadCount, ParticleCount. Overrides OnAttached, OnBind, OnSimEvent, OnStateChanged.

ElectricSfx (still : LiquidSfx): nested enum Clip { Exit, Return, Fill, Cut, TensionLoop, Caught, LoopLost, Ambient }, consts TensionLoopSeconds 0.5, AmbientLoopSeconds 4.0, AmbientPeak 0.6, static DurationOf(Clip), IsLoop(Clip), Synthesize(Clip, int sampleRate) (pure C#, deterministic); Build(int) overrides and also fills Ambient.
ElectricTheme: BloomIntensity 0.85 (was 0.9), ShaderParams documented as unused; contract colors and FillDuration 0.25 unchanged.
contract_issues: 25.4 'the droplet chain drawn with ElectricBead as fading spark dots on a dim grey cable': a bead quad knows nothing about its neighbours, so the grey cable is drawn by ElectricFx as one continuous strip along the trail from s_cut to just behind the bulb (queue 3000, under the droplets), and the droplets themselves are ElectricBead spark dots.

25.4 'small arcs jump to its own territory when within 1.5 u' is read as: distance from the orb rim to the nearest own cell (sim grid, GridQueries.NearestOwned) <= 1.5 u; at home the orb throws short arcs onto the territory around it.

25.4 'the territory flickers and blacks out': implemented at 9 Hz with at most half contrast over 0.6 s (a territory can cover much of the screen; the brief asked for comfortable flicker, no strobing).

Overlay shape ids 6-10 are used by ElectricFx through (OverlayShape)int casts; QuadBatch.OverlayShape only names 0-5. If a future shared shape takes id 6+, the electric effects would collide (suggest reserving 6-15 for biome effects).
The thin-graph rule allows position nodes; ElectricBead uses one (World) for stable per-bead seeds. No other graph property than _PIO_ShaderId, no _PIO_ global outside LiquidCommon.hlsl.
open_issues: passing = EditMode 417 (419 run, 2 skipped, TestResults/ELEC_edit.xml) + PlayMode 8 (TestResults/ELEC_play.xml). ELEC owns no test file, so no NUnit test was added; the evidence is the player probe (TestResults/ELEC_probe_electric_fps60, PASS) and the DevShots.

Not run on an Android device. The electric composite costs more ALU than the liquid one (about 6 value-noise evaluations per pixel plus hex math, more during a fill or a lightning hop) while staying in the fetch budget (5 / 6 on Medium). Perf measured only on the dev PC: avg 16.75 ms, p95 17.05 ms at the 60 fps cap, tier High. Low drops one noise octave in the micro arcs and the discharge.

Sounds checked numerically only (scratchpad dotnet harness: deterministic, no NaN, one-shots end on exact zero at peak 0.89, tension loop seam 0.072 vs neighbour steps 0.044 / 0.101 and ambience seam 0.019 vs 0.018 / 0.020, i.e. seamless); nobody listened to them yet.

Time-based effects are not in any DevShot checkpoint: the short-circuit flicker and blackout (Caught is the first frame of the elimination), the lightning hops, the crawling arcs and the 17 Hz wire jag are judged from code and single frames only.
In electric_CutDroplets the tutorial pointer ring (UI) sits exactly on the current packet, which hides part of it in that shot; the zoomed crop shows the white head at the front.

electric_SavedReturn shows a soft pink glow for about 0.12 s where the front stopped: RetractionView fades the bulb's field amplitude below 0.5 on a saved return, so the electric composite shows only the actor glow there (narrowed, still visible).
Visible but owned by others: the empty grey tutorial bubble in the saved shot (already reported by B6), the HUD danger vignette.
The scratchpad directory is shared with the parallel agents (FIRE overwrote a devshot.ps1 there); ELEC's helpers are devshot_elec.ps1, probe_elec.ps1, crop_elec.ps1 and sfxcheck/.
